text:
jess: Heads-up — during the Karpenter migration test in us-west-2 the GPU provisioner scaled up fine but ~10m later several GPU nodes terminated and pods flapped. I saw ENI allocation errors and some pods stuck Terminating. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: Ugh. Which instance types were used and were we on spot or on-demand?

jess: Multi-instance-type provisioner: p3.8xlarge, p3.2xlarge, p4d. Spot preferred with fallback to on-demand. kube events show: 
```
Warning  FailedCreatePodSandBox  2m  kubelet, ip-10-0-45-67  failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to allocate sandbox ENI: capacity exceeded
```
Also karpenter controller logs show a bunch of "insufficient resources: eni" right before node termination.

kevin: Classic ENI-per-instance limit. p3.2x and p3.8x have fairly low max ENIs for higher pod density. With GPU sharing we accidentally hit the ENI boundary. Do we have pods using hostNetwork or requiring additional ENIs?

maria: Some of the internal redis/stateful pods were hostNetwork and we had multiple sidecars that create network attachments. That bumps ENI usage.

sam: Two angles: (1) reduce pods-per-node / lower maxPods on nodeTemplate; (2) prefer instance types with higher ENI counts for high pod density (or use AWS CNI density-aware IPs). Also consider enabling pod ENI verification in the provisioner.

jess: I'm attaching the provisioner fragment we used: 
```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-test
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/capacity-type
    operator: In
    values: [spot, on-demand]
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: private-usw2
    instanceProfile: infra-worker-profile
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 30
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: 200
```
We set ttlSecondsAfterEmpty really low to speed consolidation tests. That might be causing churn.

kevin: Right — 30s TTL is aggressive for GPU jobs that have longer startup/shutdown. Also consolidation + aggressive TTL can trigger thrash. For GPUs we usually set ttlSecondsAfterEmpty >= 300 and disable consolidation during migration windows.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder — there is a pending rollout to gpu-provisioner-test from branch karpenter-migration-2 queued at 2026-02-18T09:12:03Z.

maria: Another signal: node drift — some nodes were marked NotReady briefly after creation (AWS delayed attach of ENIs), then karpenter considered them unhealthy and terminated. We should add a longer node readiness grace window.

sam: Suggested quick fixes: 
- bump ttlSecondsAfterEmpty to 300 for GPU provisioner
- add startupProbe/initialDelay for GPU init containers
- add requirement to prefer instance types with >= 8 ENIs (or explicit maxPods lower)
- add capacityType fallback to on-demand only after X minutes (avoid immediate fallback when spot brief loss occurs)

jess: I can push a patch with these changes. One more: should we set consolidation.enabled=false in Provisioner during test? That would stop Karpenter from immediately trimming nodes while they are still warming.

kevin: Yes for the migration window. Also add nodeTemplate labels/taints to separate GPU workloads so consolidation or scheduling decisions don't mix with cpu-only pools. Example taint: gpu-workload=required:NoSchedule.

maria: Economically, moving to p4d reduces instance count but hugely increases cost per hour. If ENI limits are the blocker we could instead prefer a mix of r6i for CPU-side services and smaller GPU types dedicated for single pods per node to avoid ENI exhaustion. Tradeoff: more nodes = more ENIs but because of lower pod density ENI per pod is better.

sam: For longer-term: consider using CNI enhancements (prefix delegation or trunking) or EKS Pod ENI IPv4 pod density config. Also file a ticket to AWS to see if ENI attach latency spike is expected in that AZ.

jess: Action items: 
- jess: bump TTL to 300, disable consolidation for this provisioner and add taint (I'll open PR) 
- sam: run quick cost model for p4d vs mixed-instance (ETA today afternoon)
- kevin: draft a small runbook for ENI errors and node readiness tuning (ETA tomorrow)
- maria: check events and open AWS support ticket if ENI attach latency > expected (ETA EOD)

kevin: Also one more config snippet I recommend we add to the provisioner to avoid immediate on-demand fallback: 
```
strategy:
  constraints:
    consolidation:
      enabled: false
  spotAllocation:
    fallbackDelaySeconds: 600
```
(This is conceptual; adjust to real fields)

jess: Cool. I'll push the PR and link it here. Thanks y'all :thumbsup: 

sam: Thanks — if anything flares up ping @kevin and @maria on-call.

infra-bot: incident-bot: Created incident INC-2026-034 for "ENI capacity errors causing GPU node terminations" assigned to eng-infra."
